Advertisement It is anything but. Now it's true that most of the people who stormed the border have filtered back into Morocco, but about 20-25 percent are sticking it out and making clear that they have no interest in going back home. It's also true that the border is not secure. If people decide to cross it, they can. It's just a bit harder. 🇪🇸 In Ceuta, a crowd of illegal Moroccan migrants is already establishing its own rules in the city The crowd shouts “Allahu Akbar” at National Guard officers and drags a wounded migrant through the streets in protest against being returned home. pic.twitter.com/Q27cvVFLTW — Visegrád 24 (@visegrad24) August 3, 2026 The people who left were on a lark, reveling in the violence of the mob or just enjoying the feeling of power that comes from being in a mob; but obviously quite a few of the people really wanted to leave Morocco, and it's hard to say how many are even Moroccan. This invasion was planned for quite a while, so it's quite possible that more than a few come from other countries and they are looking for an easy way to infiltrate the EU, courtesy of Sánchez. The Mayor of Ceuta says that the Sanche government is lying about how many illegal migrants have returned from Ceuta. He says that 10 000-15 000 illegal are still sleeping on the streets of Ceuta, with many of them setting up make-shift camps on the beaches. pic.twitter.com/uUOt6REVPy — Visegrád 24 (@visegrad24) August 2, 2026 Advertisement Sánchez is trying to manage the optics of the situation, and apparently sees the "crisis" as the criticism he is getting for being so soft on immigration. It doesn't appear that he thinks that open borders are the problem at all, which is why anybody to the right of Lenin is angry at him right now. Ceuta today is what El Paso was like under Biden, only worse, since it is a small enclave with no exits except back into Morocco, or onto small boats to make it to the Spanish mainland. Which, to be fair, some are taking, although I can't imagine the supply of such boats is great, and replenishment is not easy. This is today in Ceuta. Hordes of invaders are marching through the streets while chanting "There is no god but Allah", and "Allahu Akbar". Don't believe the communist regime or legacy media. In fact, his party has said outright that they are trying to replace the current set of voters with ones more amenable to the socialist agenda, which is why they just legalized about a million illegal aliens. Right now, invading Moroccans in Ceuta carry an injured man through the streets screaming “Allahu Akbar.” Dirty Sánchez says this isn't happening. pic.twitter.com/8s55sg0CCs — Tommy Robinson 🇬🇧 (@TRobinsonNewEra) August 2, 2026 Advertisement But he appears sensitive to the pressure from the European Union members who are totally freaking out. Twenty-two of the 27 EU countries have done more than express concern—they are agitating for Spain to be at least temporarily kicked out of the Schengen Zone , and a special meeting is set up for tomorrow to consider options. “Diversity is one of our main attractions and one of our strengths” Unbelievable - After 50,000 Military Age Fighting Men invaded several Spanish Enclaves - Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez is even still now repeating the Marxist Mantra pic.twitter.com/ehvfVvkEx7 — Concerned Citizen (@BGatesIsaPyscho) August 1, 2026 So Sánchez is busy spinning things and has refrained from evacuating the migrants who won't leave voluntarily to the Spanish mainland. I'm not certain how long he can hold out on that; Ceuta is small and apparently has over 10,000 or so illegal aliens roaming the streets or camped out on the beach. No doubt that some can be basically starved into leaving, but I suspect that the majority will engage in what amounts to siege warfare. You may recall he recently hosted a worldwide conference for far-left politicians and basked in the glow of the great press he was getting. He has positioned himself as the anti-Trump, and it has raised his profile and made him into a hero for the #resistance. Spanish PM Pedro Sánchez has learned a hard truth over the past few days: Once one of the EU’s most charismatic and influential leaders, he is now effectively a pariah in the bloc. That approach isn't going to work with the countries of the EU, I am pretty certain. The invasion of Ceuta has so much power to move opinion because the images were so stark, and unless he clamps down on the media and people posting videos online, it will remain an open sore. Close US President Trump said in a social media post on Sunday that an energy ceasefire had been reached between Ukraine and Russia that was "effective immediately". Ukraine's President Zelensky responded by saying his country is willing to back an energy ceasefire if Russia does the same, adding it could "become a major step toward ending the war". However, Moscow hasn't confirmed its agreement and Zelensky said Russia hit a Ukrainian power plant in Kharkiv "immediately after" Trump's post over the weekend. The BBC's Ukraine correspondent Dan Johnson reports from Kyiv, where Ukrainians are facing another winter with electricity outages that leave people without heat, light or even water.
